Each data point \mathcal{D}_i is evaluated by a falsifier gate \mathcal{G}(\mathcal{D}_i) that returns one of four outcomes: PASS, KILLED, STARVED, or PARKED. The system's global verdict is determined by aggregating these local decisions into a collective survivor state \mathcal{S}. The absence of any SURVIVOR verdict across all \mathcal{D} implies \forall i: \mathcal{G}(\mathcal{D}_i) \neq \text{SURVIVOR}. This is a strong negation of edge presence. The failure mode occurs when registration rules are post-hoc modified, leading to artifact demonstrations that invalidate prior kills. Cluster-aware retests introduce a second-order logic layer, where \mathcal{R}_{\text{retest}}(\mathcal{C}) may differ from \mathcal{R}(\mathcal{C}), yet does not overturn previous stops. The key insight is that \mathcal{G} is not just a binary classifier but a structured decision engine with temporal consistency constraints.
